main_text.p: 9. Ferrea sceptra geres, vt regum, fictile cen vas Comminuas capita.
10. Discite nunc, Reges, monitis parere, Monarchae Subdite colla iugo.
11. Iucundi seruite Deo, gaudete tremente s, Ofcula ferte pedi.
12. Ne vos disperdat furibunda in bile. Beatus Qui timet atque colit.
main_text.head: PSALMVS III. CONSTAT IX. verfibus, praeter infcriptionem.
main_text.p: 1. QVam multi vndique multa comminantur! Quam densa, o Deus, extulere signa!
2. Papae quas video hostium phalanges, Quot currus, galeas, manus, fecures!
3. Dicunt insuper, a Deo est relictus. Nugantur. Deus est mea salutis
4. Lorica & clypeus, potenfque vallum, Qui regis caput erigit superbum.
5. Clamaui ad Dominum frequenter orans, Respondítque mihi e iugo Sionis.
6. Posti stratus iacui fopore blando, Meas ante fores Deo excubante.
7. Etsi mille decem irruant cohortes, Me striclim obsideant, nihil verebor.
8. Exurge, o Deus, hostibus reuinclis Impingas colaphos, genas retunde.

page.notes: Printed text appears to be a 17th-century Latin edition (Cantica Sacra). Line 1 of Psalm III has a damaged or uncertain spelling in places. Doubtful readings: "Posti" (likely "Postquam", line 6 header is partly cut), "fopore" (likely "sopore"), "Papae" (likely "Ecce" or "Papae" as printed), "cen" (printed as "cen", probably "ceu"), "Comminuas" (likely "Comminuas"), "monitis", "relictus" and "Nugantur" are as read. Words marked with uncertainty have not been tagged with [?] because the scan is clear enough to read them; the stanza 9 of Psalm III is a continued line and the page ends there. Lines of the Psalm are printed as verse lines, here joined into stanzas as printed.
